tara: FYI I enabled sparrow9b.int4 on the long-summary route (canary 6%). Early evals show clear token-economy wins but a reproducible temporal-reference drift in multi-step summaries (dates/timelines shift by a step).

ben: Can you paste a sanitized failure + traffic profile?

tara: Example:
```
INPUT: 4k token project log
PROMPT: extract timeline (steps=2) then summarize
FP16: timeline: 2024-06-01 -> planning; 2024-06-15 -> launch
INT4: timeline: 2024-06-15 -> planning; 2024-06-01 -> launch  // swapped events
```
Traffic: tokens_in ~4000, steps=2, prefix_cache=true, canary=6%. Unit costs: fp16 $0.027/request, int8 $0.0135, int4 $0.0047.

ops-bot: eval alert: long-timeline-slice fail rate rose 1.3% -> 5.9% on sparrow9b.int4 (threshold 2%). kv_alignment metric down 1.2%.

lucy: This looks like accumulated KV quantization error affecting positional consistency across chained ops. Disabling prefix_cache for int4 reduced the issue in staging by ~1.0pt but didn't close gap.

ben: Proposed quick mitigation: routing rule based on tokens_in OR steps: if tokens_in>3000 OR steps>=2 -> sparrow9b.int8 else sparrow9b.int4. Also add per-route metric factuality_drift and kv_alignment with a rollback trigger: factuality_drift > 2% AND delta_vs_baseline > 1% over 20m.

tara: GTN blurb draft for product: "Recommendation: Default sparrow9b.int4 for short single-pass summarization to capture ~60-65% cost savings vs int8. Route multi-step or high-token timelines to int8 by default to avoid temporal drift. Unit-econ snapshot: fp16 ~$0.027, int8 ~$0.0135, int4 ~$0.0047 per high-token request; expected UX risk if misrouted: temporal ordering errors in ~4-7% of multi-step calls."

lucy: Ops rollout checklist: (1) deploy routing policy behind feature flag; (2) disable prefix_cache for int4 until validated; (3) run 8h A/B smoke with synthetic timeline-heavy traffic at 10% traffic; (4) monitor factuality_drift/kv_alignment/p95 latency; (5) auto-pin to int8 on rollback trigger.

ben: I'll open the routing PR + attach failing examples and eval diffs. Tagging @gtn for product copy.

gtn: Thanks, looks good. We'll wait for smoke results before any public GTN note. Please include the exact unit-econ numbers in the PR so we can surface them in the release doc.
